entities.summary: Concha Michel (1899–1990) was a Mexican singer-songwriter, political activist, playwright, and a researcher who published several projects on the culture of indigenous communities. She was one of the few women who performed in the corrido style. She created the Institute of Folklore in Michoacan and was one of the first collectors of folklore and preservers of the traditions of the Mexican people. She was a cultural icon having relationships with two presidents, and a broad range of Mexico's most prominent artists including Diego Rivera, Frida Kahlo, Guadalupe Marín, Tina Modotti, Elena Poniatowska, Anita Brenner and others.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: As a cultural icon and researcher, Concha Michel played a crucial role in preserving Mexico's indigenous traditions through her work at the Institute of Folklore. Her contributions to the field of folklore have had a lasting impact on Mexican identity and culture.
